text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The Reform Party council decided to leave the ruling coalition because of the cooperation agreement between the Coalition Party and the Centre Party. It is not yet known, whether the Centre Party will replace them in the governmment.
- Parliament decided to increase pensions by 100 kroons from January 1.
- A border guard officer serving as a lecturer at the National Defence Academy has been arrested in a bribery case. He allegedly took bribe for smuggling in a container of cigarettes.

- Director of the Kreenholm textile plant in the northestern town of Narva announced that no agreement on the increase of wages has been reached and that the trade union wage raise demands will result in the dismissal of some staff.
- Imre Perli, the computer hacker suspected of having sold illegal data bases with confidential information, gave himself up to the police.

- Estonian and Danish transport ministers agreed in Helsinki on the sharing of the Tallinn-Copenhagen and Tallinn-Stockholm lines by the aviation companies SAS and Estonian Air, owned by Maersk. An agreement has also reached with Lithuania on flights between Tallinn and Vilnius.
